About us

Auckland Council serves over 1.5 million Aucklanders providing services, policies and decision-making. We’re here to serve Auckland and build a more prosperous region, one that gives a voice to our citizens, and makes it a great place to live, visit and invest. Our talented people support Auckland’s elected representatives by providing specialist advice, implementing decisions and delivering services like rubbish and recycling, resource and building consents, bylaws, events and parks. Our vision is to create a world-class city where talent wants to live. If you are interested in working for Auckland, visit our career website (careers.aucklandcouncil.govt.nz) or check our 'Jobs' and 'Life' tabs. Auckland Transport, Tātaki Auckland Unlimited, Watercare are independent council-controlled organisations that look after specific council assets or activities on our behalf.

    Got an idea to help reduce waste in your community, school or business? ♻️ The 2026 Waste Minimisation and Innovation Fund is open for projects that help Auckland reuse more, recycle better and move closer to our goal of zero waste by 2040. 📝 Apply from 1 August to 31 August 2026 here: https://lnkd.in/ee7JsBxP #OurAkl #Auckland #Waste #ZeroWaste #Fund

    Great news, Auckland's long-fought local alcohol policy is showing promising results after its first year and we're moving in the right direction. ✅ Police data shows alcohol-related harm incidents in Auckland have been trending downward since peaking in 2023. In 2025 there were seven per cent fewer reported incidents than in 2024. ✅ Police also saw fewer aggravated robberies of bottle shops, which historically occurred most frequently between 9pm and 11pm. ✅ Early analysis indicates rates of alcohol-related emergency department presentations at Auckland City Hospital were lower in the year after shorter trading hours for alcohol outlets came into effect, compared to the year before. ✅ Community members are reporting less noise, less violence and safer neighbourhoods. They said the policy gave them a stronger ability to influence alcohol licensing decisions in their local areas. For context, the policy came into force in 2024 and introduced measures to reduce alcohol-related harm, like tougher licensing rules and shorter trading hours for businesses selling alcohol. ℹ️ Find out more results from the first annual report: https://lnkd.in/e_ieqKDR #Auckland #OurAkl #AlcoholPolicy #Report

    Proposed changes to Plan Change 120 have been approved today, giving Aucklanders another opportunity to have their say on the region’s housing rules. The proposal continues to provide significant housing capacity where it makes the most sense - close to public transport, jobs and services. It also means eighty-five percent of properties won't be affected. Public submissions are expected to open late August 2026. ℹ️ Find out more about the proposal here: https://lnkd.in/ePxfN4cv #OurAkl #Auckland #PC120

    Applications for this year’s Regional Historic Heritage Grant Programme funding round are now open until 14 September 2026. The funding priorities include: ✅ Conservation of regionally significant historic heritage places, including places in an historic heritage area. ✅ Conservation of at-risk historic heritage places, including initiatives which address the impacts of climate change. ✅ Supporting kaitiakitanga of Māori cultural heritage places. Want to apply but not sure how? Learn more about these grants and the application process at an online workshop. 📅 Wednesday 5 August 2026 ℹ️ Find out more: https://lnkd.in/eHUvnfaE 📷 The former Church of Ascension in Point Chevalier after an exterior re-paint thanks to a previous funding round of this grant. #Auckland #HeritageAKL #Grants #Funding
